correctness.rationale: After annular rescaling, the phase has large parameter \(\lambda_R=\gamma(\log R)^{\gamma-1}\) multiplying a smooth phase converging in sufficiently high \(C^N\) to \(\log|\eta|\), whose Hessian is nondegenerate on the fixed annulus. Choosing Fourier data that cancels the multiplier phase and decay makes the output a fixed nonzero Schwartz function, while uniform stationary phase gives input \(L^p\)-norm at most \(C(\log R)^\beta\lambda_R^{-d/2+d/p}\) for \(p>2\). This yields the displayed lower norm power. For \(p<2\), duality applies to the conjugate multiplier with the same phase curvature and decay. Thus any negative logarithmic exponent of the localized norm contradicts uniform multiplier boundedness. The argument is scale-uniform and does not rely on finite experiments.

final_claim: For \(\gamma>1\), \(\beta\ge0\), and \(1<p<\infty\) with \(p\ne2\), boundedness on \(L^p(\mathbb R^d)\) of the logarithmic oscillatory multiplier \(m_{\gamma,\beta}(\xi)=L(\xi)^{-\beta}e^{iL(\xi)^\gamma}\) forces \(\beta\ge d(\gamma-1)|1/2-1/p|\); more quantitatively, every fixed-annular localization at radius \(R\) has operator norm at least a constant times \((\log R)^{d(\gamma-1)|1/2-1/p|-\beta}\).
limitations: The statement is a necessary below-endpoint obstruction; it does not settle strong boundedness on the critical equality line.
